## ✨ Highlights

HAProxy reloads that reset nothing, and a Let's Encrypt fix for nodes
that remove a certificate.

- 🔁 **Reloads hand the listeners over**: when a configuration is
  applied, the previous HAProxy process now passes its listening sockets
  to the new one instead of closing them. New connections that arrived
  just as it reloaded used to be reset: 10 to 76 failed requests per 45
  reloads at 12,000 to 35,000 requests a second. **None** fail now.
- 📜 **Removing a Let's Encrypt certificate no longer hangs the node**:
  `janusctl haproxy acme check` or `acme apply` without one of the
  certificates never returned, and the node's certificate management
  stayed stuck until janusd restarted.
- 📦 **Prometheus node_exporter 1.13.1**.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **A node hit by the Let's Encrypt hang** (a certificate removal that
  timed out, `ACMEApplyConfig: ... DeadlineExceeded`): update it, then
  remove the certificate again. Its next boot puts back the certificate's
  file the hung removal had set aside. Until a node runs this release,
  don't remove a certificate from its Let's Encrypt configuration. If
  one is stuck already: drain it if it's a cluster member, run `janusctl
  -n NODE system restart`, then undrain it.
- Nothing to change in your HAProxy configurations for the reloads.

## 🔁 HAProxy reloads

- **The listeners are handed over at a reload**
  ([#680](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/680)). Before, the new
  HAProxy process bound its own listeners next to the previous one's,
  then the previous one closed its listeners. Connections still waiting
  in its queue were reset: established but not accepted yet, or still
  in their handshake. `option idle-close-on-response`
  ([v2026.11.18](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/releases/tag/v2026.11.18))
  only covers the connections HAProxy had already accepted. janusd now
  uses HAProxy's own seamless reload. The previous process exposes its
  listeners on a socket of janusd's (`expose-fd listeners`), the new one
  takes them (`-x`), and none is ever closed. Measured on 3.4 with a new
  connection per request straight to HAProxy: across 45 reloads at
  12,000 to 35,000 requests a second, 10 to 76 requests failed before,
  **none** now. Your `haproxy.cfg` doesn't change: the socket is
  declared in a file of janusd's (`janus-handover.cfg`), root-only, and
  a configuration still can't declare one itself. Whoever reaches such a
  socket could take the listeners.
- **A reload that changes how the listeners are opened opens new ones**,
  so the change applies. A socket handed over keeps its backlog and the
  other settings it was opened with. This covers a `bind` line, a
  `backlog` or `maxconn`, the threads, a `tune.*` setting and
  `net.core.somaxconn`. The first reload after janusd restarts also
  opens new listeners.
- **`net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req` is on at every boot**: on those reloads,
  the connections queued on a listener that closes move to the new
  process's instead of being reset. In the same measurements it cut the
  failures to 0-2 per 45 reloads.
- [Reloads and idle connections](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/haproxy-config.md#reloads-and-idle-connections)
  explains both.

## 📜 Let's Encrypt

- **Removing a certificate deadlocked the node's ACME manager**
  ([#694](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/694)). Checking or
  applying a Let's Encrypt configuration without one of the
  certificates never returned (`DeadlineExceeded`). From then on, every
  `acme status`/`get`/`check`/`apply` timed out, nothing was renewed,
  and any HAProxy validation or reload on that node would have hung
  too. A cluster member pulling such a configuration from its orderer
  hung the same way, and so could an ordinary `acme apply` that
  happened during a reload. Only a janusd restart cleared it, and the
  certificate's file stayed set aside in `/etc/haproxy/.acme-removing/`.
  The node now checks the removal without the deadlock, and its boot
  puts such a file back, or deletes it when the certificate is no longer
  configured.

## 📦 Components

- **Prometheus node_exporter 1.13.0 → 1.13.1** (the
  `prometheus-node-exporter` extension). It fixes the btrfs and textfile
  collectors, neither of which Janus turns on. No security fix.

## 🧪 Tests

- `qemu-acme-test` removes a certificate, with each call bounded: refused
  while `haproxy.cfg` uses it, accepted once it doesn't. On v2026.11.19-3
  it fails with the production error.
- `qemu-system-api-test` checks that every reload hands the listeners
  over when it changes no listener, and opens new ones when it does.
  After a janusd restart, the takeover opens new listeners and the next
  reload hands them over. A Go test with the real HAProxy reloads 20
  times under a load of new connections: 0 failed with the hand-over,
  21 without it.
